items.title: Cascadu interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, November 15, 2019
items.q: I drove four hours to Baltimore to see and meet one of the guys who I revered for his cosmic — he was my cosmic jazz master.

ctx.x: I don’t. Because I recognize that everybody is coming from a different place you know. There is tolerance and there is leading by example. And I’ve always believed that if your character and if your composure can speak for you in what it is you are doing then somehow or the other you’re going to touch that life and people are going to remember and take something with you. And it doesn’t matter what they take as long as they take something with you and it helps to transform their lives or their thinking or their…

and you come to a concert or something and you hear something that’s really beautiful and in your deepest and darkest moment you remember that experience that caused you such elation at that point in time. Take a piece of it with you. Take it with you you know. Let it manifest, let it change your life. We are not here — we are the soldiers for peace and harmony and for a better world. When, I always remember, you know that poem if the rest of the world is losing their head and you can keep your head about you…
